resolutions.researcher_notes: Seed cite (youm7, 2021-01-21) lists 'khat izdiwaj Damietta / Fenosa' (Fenosa = Union Fenosa Gas, SEGAS's Spanish partner — confirms this IS the Damietta–SEGAS line, not a naming coincidence) among national gas-grid duplication lines completed/underway c.2021, matching GEM's 12km/42in specs exactly. Attaqa.net (2023) independently confirms the Damietta LNG complex (which this feeder/duplication line serves) is actively operating and exporting as of 2023. No source contradicts 'operating'.

Definitional: the article's entire subject is 'al-shabaka al-qawmiyya lil-ghazat al-tabi'iyya' (national natural gas network) and the line is listed as a 'khat ghaz' (gas line). Single direct source but the fact is self-evident from the pipeline's own name/context; no ambiguity or contradiction found.

Youm7 lists this 42-inch line as part of a package reinforcing/'doubling' ('izdiwaj') the national high-pressure gas grid; Wikipedia's GASCO article independently confirms GASCO's mandate is national gas transmission (as opposed to local distribution). 42-inch trunk diameter is itself consistent with transmission, not a distribution lateral.

Youm7 (dated 2021-01-21) lists the Damietta/Fenosa duplication line among gas-grid projects underway/completed circa 2020-2021. Wikipedia's SEGAS LNG page independently confirms the SEGAS plant (which this line feeds) resumed gas supply/operations in February 2021 after an idle period — corroborated further by Eni's March-2021 press release and Daily News Egypt's Dec-2020 report of the planned Q1 2021 restart. These confirm 2021 as the correct window but describe the LNG plant restart rather than this specific pipeline segment's commissioning date — flagging this distinction for the record, though it is consistent with GEM's existing StartYear1=2021.

Exact text: 'khat izdiwaj Damietta / Fenosa bi-tul 12 km - qutr 42" taklifat al-mashruʿ: 340 million EGP'. Only one working source found with this precise 12km figure despite extensive searching (petroleum.gov.eg overview PDF, petro-news.com, egy-map.com, presidency.eg all cover OTHER Damietta-area gas lines, e.g. the distinct 34km Gamsa-Fenosa line to West Damietta power station — confirms this dataset's methodology/naming convention is sound, but doesn't independently corroborate the 12km figure itself). Single strong (ministry-sourced) source → medium tier, not low.

Same passage as Length: 'qutr 42"' for the Damietta/Fenosa duplication line. Only one working source found with the exact diameter figure (see Length notes for search exhaustiveness); single strong ministry-sourced article → medium tier.

The line is named/located as a Damietta grid-reinforcement ('izdiwaj') project drawing on the national gas network at Damietta; consistent with GEM's FuelSource='Damietta'. Single direct source; no conflicting attribution found (e.g. no source ties feedgas here to a named offshore field instead of the domestic grid hub).

Youm7 explicitly names/locates the line as 'Damietta / Fenosa'; Wikipedia's SEGAS LNG page independently confirms the SEGAS complex the line feeds sits in (New) Damietta, ~60km west of Port Said, Damietta Governorate, Egypt — matching GEM's StartLocation/EndLocation/State/Country values exactly. Two independent, unambiguous sources.

No source ties ownership of this specific 12km segment to a named party; instead this corroborates GEM's standing Owner-vs-Operator convention for Egyptian national trunk lines. Wikipedia's GASCO article states GASCO ('Operator' per gem.wiki) is a subsidiary of, and majority (70%) owned by, the Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Company (EGAS) — matching GEM's Owner1='Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co' 100%. EGAS's own site (egas.com.eg) independently confirms the corporate relationship, listing GASCO as one of its subsidiaries/quick-links. Note: could not verify Lexology's 'GASCO acts on behalf of EGAS' summary directly — that page returned HTTP 403 and was excluded per the working-URL requirement.
